segs.p: Saṁyojanasutta
segs.e: The Fetter

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ sambahulā therā bhikkhū macchikāsaṇḍe viharanti ambāṭakavane.
segs.e: At one time several senior mendicants were staying near Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Wild Mango Grove.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulānaṁ therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantānaṁ maṇḍalamāḷe sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: Now at that time, after the meal, on return from almsround, several senior mendicants sat together in the pavilion and this discussion came up among them:

segs.p: “‘saṁyojanan’ti vā, āvuso, ‘saṁyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā nānābyañjanā udāhu ekatthā byañjanameva nānan”ti?
segs.e: “Reverends, the ‘fetter’ and the ‘things that tighten the fetters’: do these things differ in both meaning and phrasing? Or do they mean the same thing, and differ only in the phrasing?”

segs.p: Tatrekaccehi therehi bhikkhūhi evaṁ byākataṁ hoti:
segs.e: Some senior mendicants answered like this:

segs.p: “‘saṁyojanan’ti vā, āvuso, ‘saṁyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā cā”ti.
segs.e: “Reverends, the ‘fetter’ and the ‘things that tighten the fetters’: these things differ in both meaning and phrasing.”

segs.p: Ekaccehi therehi bhikkhūhi evaṁ byākataṁ hoti:
segs.e: But some senior mendicants answered like this:

segs.p: “‘saṁyojanan’ti vā, āvuso, ‘saṁyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nānan”ti.
segs.e: “Reverends, the ‘fetter’ and the ‘things that tighten the fetters’ mean the same thing; they differ only in the phrasing.”

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena citto gahapati migapathakaṁ anuppatto hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena.
segs.e: Now at that time the householder Citta had arrived at Migapathaka on some business.

segs.p: Assosi kho citto gahapati sambahulānaṁ kira therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantānaṁ maṇḍalamāḷe sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: He heard about what those senior mendicants were discussing.

segs.p: “‘saṁyojanan’ti vā, āvuso, ‘saṁyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā nānābyañjanā udāhu ekatthā byañjanameva nānan”ti?
Tatrekaccehi therehi bhikkhūhi evaṁ byākataṁ:
“‘saṁyojanan’ti vā, āvuso, ‘saṁyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā cā”ti.
Ekaccehi therehi bhikkhūhi evaṁ byākataṁ:
“‘saṁyojanan’ti vā, āvuso, ‘saṁyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nānan”ti.
Atha kho citto gahapati yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho citto gahapati there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: So he went up to them, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to them,

segs.p: “sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante, sambahulānaṁ kira therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantānaṁ maṇḍalamāḷe sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: “Sirs, I heard that you were discussing whether the ‘fetter’ and the ‘things that tighten the fetters’ differ in both meaning and phrasing, or whether they mean the same thing, and differ only in the phrasing.”

segs.p: ‘saṁyojanan’ti vā, āvuso, ‘saṁyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā nānābyañjanā udāhu ekatthā byañjanameva nānan”ti?
Ekaccehi therehi bhikkhūhi evaṁ byākataṁ:
“‘saṁyojanan’ti vā, āvuso, ‘saṁyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā cā”ti.
Ekaccehi therehi bhikkhūhi evaṁ byākataṁ “‘saṁyojanan’ti vā, āvuso, ‘saṁyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nānan”ti.
“Evaṁ, gahapatī”ti.
segs.e: “That’s right, householder.”

segs.p: “‘Saṁyojanan’ti vā, bhante, ‘saṁyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā ca.
segs.e: “Sirs, the ‘fetter’ and the ‘things that tighten the fetters’: these things differ in both meaning and phrasing.

segs.p: Tena hi, bhante, upamaṁ vo karissāmi.
segs.e: Well then, sirs, I shall give you a simile.

segs.p: Upamāyapidhekacce viññū purisā bhāsitassa atthaṁ ājānanti.
segs.e: For by means of a simile some sensible people understand the meaning of what is said.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, kāḷo ca balībaddo odāto ca balībaddo ekena dāmena vā yottena vā saṁyuttā assu.
segs.e: Suppose there was a black ox and a white ox yoked by a single harness or yoke.

segs.p: Yo nu kho evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Would it be right to say that

segs.p: ‘kāḷo balībaddo odātassa balībaddassa saṁyojanaṁ, odāto balībaddo kāḷassa balībaddassa saṁyojanan’ti, sammā nu kho so vadamāno vadeyyā”ti?
segs.e: the black ox is the yoke of the white ox, or the white ox is the yoke of the black ox?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, gahapati.
segs.e: “No, householder.

segs.p: Na kho, gahapati, kāḷo balībaddo odātassa balībaddassa saṁyojanaṁ, napi odāto balībaddo kāḷassa balībaddassa saṁyojanaṁ;
segs.e: The black ox is not the yoke of the white ox, nor is the white ox the yoke of the black ox.

segs.p: yena kho te ekena dāmena vā yottena vā saṁyuttā taṁ tattha saṁyojanan”ti.
segs.e: The yoke there is the single harness or yoke that they’re yoked by.”

segs.p: “Evameva kho, bhante, na cakkhu rūpānaṁ saṁyojanaṁ, na rūpā cakkhussa saṁyojanaṁ;
segs.e: “In the same way, the eye is not the fetter of sights, nor are sights the fetter of the eye.

segs.p: yañca tattha tadubhayaṁ paṭicca uppajjati chandarāgo taṁ tattha saṁyojanaṁ.
segs.e: The fetter there is the desire and greed that arises from the pair of them.

segs.p: Na sotaṁ saddānaṁ …
segs.e: The ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: na ghānaṁ gandhānaṁ …
na jivhā rasānaṁ …
na kāyo phoṭṭhabbānaṁ saṁyojanaṁ, na phoṭṭhabbā kāyassa saṁyojanaṁ;
yañca tattha tadubhayaṁ paṭicca uppajjati chandarāgo taṁ tattha saṁyojanaṁ.
Na mano dhammānaṁ saṁyojanaṁ, na dhammā manassa saṁyojanaṁ;
segs.e: mind is not the fetter of ideas, nor are ideas the fetter of the mind.

segs.p: yañca tattha tadubhayaṁ paṭicca uppajjati chandarāgo taṁ tattha saṁyojanan”ti.
segs.e: The fetter there is the desire and greed that arises from the pair of them.”

segs.p: “Lābhā te, gahapati, suladdhaṁ te, gahapati,
segs.e: “You’re fortunate, householder, so very fortunate,

segs.p: yassa te gambhīre buddhavacane paññācakkhu kamatī”ti.
segs.e: to traverse the Buddha’s deep teachings with the eye of wisdom.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.

segs.p: Paṭhamaisidattasutta
segs.e: With Isidatta (1st)

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ sambahulā therā bhikkhū macchikāsaṇḍe viharanti ambāṭakavane.
segs.e: At one time several senior mendicants were staying near Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Wild Mango Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho citto gahapati there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Citta the householder went up to them, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to them,

segs.p: “adhivāsentu me, bhante, therā svātanāya bhattan”ti.
segs.e: “Sirs, would the senior monks please accept tomorrow’s meal from me?”

segs.p: Adhivāsesuṁ kho therā bhikkhū tuṇhībhāvena.
segs.e: They consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ adhivāsanaṁ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Knowing that the senior mendicants had consented, Citta rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled them, keeping them on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho therā bhikkhū tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena cittassa gahapatissa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: Then when the night had passed, the senior mendicants robed up in the morning and, taking their bowls and robes, went to Citta’s home, and sat down on the seats spread out.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṁ theraṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Citta went up to them, bowed, sat down to one side, and asked the senior venerable,

segs.p: “‘dhātunānattaṁ, dhātunānattan’ti, bhante thera, vuccati.
segs.e: “Honorable Senior, they speak of ‘the diversity of elements’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhātunānattaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: In what way did the Buddha speak of the diversity of elements?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā thero tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: When he said this, the senior venerable kept silent.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṁ theraṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time …

segs.p: “‘dhātunānattaṁ, dhātunānattan’ti, bhante thera, vuccati.
Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhātunānattaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā”ti?
Dutiyampi kho āyasmā thero tuṇhī ahosi.
Tatiyampi kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṁ theraṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And for a third time, Citta asked him,

segs.p: “‘dhātunānattaṁ, dhātunānattan’ti, bhante thera, vuccati.
segs.e: “Honorable Senior, they speak of ‘the diversity of elements’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhātunānattaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: In what way did the Buddha speak of the diversity of elements?”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho āyasmā thero tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: And a second time and a third time the senior venerable kept silent.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā isidatto tasmiṁ bhikkhusaṅghe sabbanavako hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Isidatta was the most junior mendicant in that Saṅgha.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā isidatto āyasmantaṁ theraṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: He said to the senior venerable,

segs.p: “byākaromahaṁ, bhante thera, cittassa gahapatino etaṁ pañhan”ti?
segs.e: “Honorable Senior, may I answer Citta’s question?”

segs.p: “Byākarohi tvaṁ, āvuso isidatta, cittassa gahapatino etaṁ pañhan”ti.
segs.e: “Answer it, Reverend Isidatta.”

segs.p: “Evañhi tvaṁ, gahapati, pucchasi:
segs.e: “Householder, is this your question:

segs.p: ‘dhātunānattaṁ, dhātunānattanti, bhante thera, vuccati.
segs.e: ‘They speak of “the diversity of elements”.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhātunānattaṁ, vuttaṁ bhagavatā’”ti?
segs.e: In what way did the Buddha speak of the diversity of elements?’”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Idaṁ kho, gahapati, dhātunānattaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā—
segs.e: “This is the diversity of elements spoken of by the Buddha.

segs.p: cakkhudhātu, rūpadhātu, cakkhuviññāṇadhātu …pe…
segs.e: The eye element, the sights element, the eye consciousness element …

segs.p: manodhātu, dhammadhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu.
segs.e: The mind element, the idea element, the mind consciousness element.

segs.p: Ettāvatā kho, gahapati, dhātunānattaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā”ti.
segs.e: This is how the Buddha spoke of the diversity of elements.”

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati āyasmato isidattassa bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā there bhikkhū paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi.
segs.e: Then Citta, having approved and agreed with what Isidatta said, served and satisfied the senior mendicants with his own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: Atha kho therā bhikkhū bhuttāvino onītapattapāṇino uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṁsu.
segs.e: When the senior mendicants had eaten and washed their hands and bowls, they rose from their seats and left.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā thero āyasmantaṁ isidattaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the senior venerable said to Venerable Isidatta,

segs.p: “sādhu kho taṁ, āvuso isidatta, eso pañho paṭibhāsi, neso pañho maṁ paṭibhāsi.
segs.e: “Isidatta, it’s good that you felt inspired to answer that question, because I didn’t.

segs.p: Tenahāvuso isidatta, yadā aññathāpi evarūpo pañho āgaccheyya, taññevettha paṭibhāseyyā”ti.
segs.e: So when a similar question comes up, you should also answer it as you feel inspired.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.

segs.e: With Isidatta (2nd)

segs.p: “yā imā, bhante thera, anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke uppajjanti:
segs.e: “Honorable Senior, there are many different views that arise in the world. For example:

segs.p: ‘sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīranti vā, aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā.
segs.e: the cosmos is eternal, or not eternal, or finite, or infinite; the soul and the body are one and the same, or the soul is one thing, the body another; after death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists.

segs.p: Yāni cimāni dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni brahmajāle bhaṇitāni;
segs.e: And also the sixty-two misconceptions spoken of in ‘The Divine Net’.

segs.p: imā nu kho, bhante, diṭṭhiyo kismiṁ sati honti, kismiṁ asati na hontī”ti?
segs.e: When what exists do these views come to be? When what doesn’t exist do these views not come to be?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā thero tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: When he said this, the senior venerable kept silent.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho citto gahapati …pe…
segs.e: For a second time …

segs.p: tatiyampi kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṁ theraṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And for a third time, Citta said to him:

segs.p: “yā imā, bhante thera, anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke uppajjanti—
segs.e: “Honorable Senior, there are many different views that arise in the world. …

segs.p: sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīranti vā, aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā.
Yāni cimāni dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni brahmajāle bhaṇitāni;
imā nu kho, bhante, diṭṭhiyo kismiṁ sati honti, kismiṁ asati na hontī”ti?
segs.e: When what exists do these views come to be? When what doesn’t exist do these views not come to be?”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho āyasmā thero tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: And a second time and a third time the senior venerable kept silent.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā isidatto tasmiṁ bhikkhusaṅghe sabbanavako hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Isidatta was the most junior mendicant in that Saṅgha.

segs.e: He said to the senior venerable,

segs.e: “Answer it, Reverend Isidatta.”

segs.p: “Evañhi tvaṁ, gahapati, pucchasi:
segs.e: “Householder, is this your question:

segs.p: ‘yā imā, bhante thera, anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke uppajjanti—
segs.e: ‘There are many different views that arise in the world …

segs.p: sassato lokoti vā …pe…;
imā nu kho, bhante, diṭṭhiyo kismiṁ sati honti, kismiṁ asati na hontī’”ti?
segs.e: When what exists do these views come to be? When what doesn’t exist do these views not come to be?’”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yā imā, gahapati, anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke uppajjanti:
segs.e: “Householder, there are many different views that arise in the world. For example:

segs.p: ‘sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā anantavā lokoti vā, taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīranti vā, aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti vā.
segs.e: the cosmos is eternal, or not eternal, or finite, or infinite; the soul and the body are one and the same, or the soul is one thing, the body another; after death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists.

segs.e: And also the sixty-two misconceptions spoken of in ‘The Divine Net’.

segs.p: imā kho, gahapati, diṭṭhiyo sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā sati honti, sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā asati na hontī’”ti.
segs.e: These views come to be when substantialist view exists. When substantialist view does not exist they do not come to be.”

segs.p: “Kathaṁ pana, bhante, sakkāyadiṭṭhi hotī”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, how does substantialist view come about?”

segs.p: “Idha, gahapati, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṁ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṁ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto
segs.e: “It’s when an unlearned ordinary person has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the true persons.

segs.p: rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ;
segs.e: They regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

segs.p: vedanaṁ attato samanupassati …pe…
segs.e: They regard feeling …

segs.p: saññaṁ …
segs.e: perception …

segs.p: saṅkhāre …
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, attani vā viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapati, sakkāyadiṭṭhi hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how substantialist view comes about.”

segs.p: “Kathaṁ pana, bhante, sakkāyadiṭṭhi na hotī”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, how does substantialist view not come about?”

segs.p: “Idha, gahapati, sutavā ariyasāvako ariyānaṁ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto sappurisānaṁ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto
segs.e: “It’s when a learned noble disciple has seen the noble ones, and is skilled and trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve seen true persons, and are skilled and trained in the teaching of the true persons.

segs.p: na rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, na attani vā rūpaṁ, na rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ;
segs.e: They don’t regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

segs.p: na vedanaṁ …
segs.e: They don’t regard feeling …

segs.p: na saññaṁ …
segs.e: perception …

segs.p: na saṅkhāre …
segs.e: choices …

segs.p: na viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ, na attani vā viññāṇaṁ, na viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
segs.e: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapati, sakkāyadiṭṭhi na hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how substantialist view does not come about.”

segs.p: “Kuto, bhante, ayyo isidatto āgacchatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, where has Master Isidatta come from?”

segs.p: “Avantiyā kho, gahapati, āgacchāmī”ti.
segs.e: “I come from Avanti, householder.”

segs.p: “Atthi, bhante, avantiyā isidatto nāma kulaputto amhākaṁ adiṭṭhasahāyo pabbajito?
segs.e: “Sir, there’s a friend of mine named Isidatta who I’ve never met. He’s gone forth from a good family in Avanti.

segs.p: Diṭṭho so āyasmatā”ti?
segs.e: Have you met him?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, gahapatī”ti.
segs.e: “Yes, householder.”

segs.p: “Kahaṁ nu kho so, bhante, āyasmā etarahi viharatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, where is that venerable now staying?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā isidatto tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: When he said this, Isidatta kept silent.

segs.p: “Ayyo no, bhante, isidatto”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, are you that Isidatta?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, gahapatī”ti.
segs.e: “Yes, householder.”

segs.p: “Abhiramatu, bhante, ayyo isidatto macchikāsaṇḍe.
segs.e: “Sir, I hope Master Isidatta is happy here in Macchikāsaṇḍa,

segs.p: Ramaṇīyaṁ ambāṭakavanaṁ.
segs.e: for the Wild Mango Grove is lovely.

segs.p: Ahaṁ ayyassa isidattassa ussukkaṁ karissāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānan”ti.
segs.e: I’ll make sure that Master Isidatta is provided with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.”

segs.p: “Kalyāṇaṁ vuccati, gahapatī”ti.
segs.e: “That’s nice of you to say, householder.”

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati āyasmato isidattassa bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā there bhikkhū paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi.
segs.e: Then Citta, having approved and agreed with what Isidatta said, served and satisfied the senior mendicants with his own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: Atha kho therā bhikkhū bhuttāvino onītapattapāṇino uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṁsu.
segs.e: When the senior mendicants had eaten and washed their hands and bowls, they rose from their seats and left.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā thero āyasmantaṁ isidattaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the senior venerable said to Venerable Isidatta,

segs.p: “sādhu kho taṁ, āvuso isidatta, eso pañho paṭibhāsi.
segs.e: “Isidatta, it’s good that you felt inspired to answer that question, because I didn’t.

segs.p: Neso pañho maṁ paṭibhāsi.
Tenahāvuso isidatta, yadā aññathāpi evarūpo pañho āgaccheyya, taññevettha paṭibhāseyyā”ti.
segs.e: So when a similar question comes up, you should also answer it as you feel inspired.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā isidatto senāsanaṁ saṁsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya macchikāsaṇḍamhā pakkāmi.
segs.e: But Isidatta set his lodgings in order and, taking his bowl and robe, left Macchikāsaṇḍa,

segs.p: Yaṁ macchikāsaṇḍamhā pakkāmi, tathā pakkantova ahosi, na puna paccāgacchīti.
segs.e: never to return.

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.

segs.p: Mahakapāṭihāriyasutta
segs.e: Mahaka’s Demonstration

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ sambahulā therā bhikkhū macchikāsaṇḍe viharanti ambāṭakavane.
segs.e: At one time several senior mendicants were staying near Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Wild Mango Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho citto gahapati there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Citta the householder went up to them, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to them,

segs.p: “adhivāsentu me, bhante, therā svātanāya gokule bhattan”ti.
segs.e: “Sirs, would the senior monks please accept tomorrow’s meal from me in my milkshed?”

segs.p: Adhivāsesuṁ kho therā bhikkhū tuṇhībhāvena.
segs.e: They consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ adhivāsanaṁ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then, knowing that the senior mendicants had consented, Citta rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled them, keeping them on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho therā bhikkhū tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena cittassa gahapatino gokulaṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: Then when the night had passed, the senior mendicants robed up in the morning and, taking their bowls and robes, went to Citta’s milkshed, and sat down on the seats spread out.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati there bhikkhū paṇītena sappipāyāsena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi.
segs.e: Then Citta served and satisfied the senior mendicants with his own hands with delicious milk-rice made with ghee.

segs.p: Atha kho therā bhikkhū bhuttāvino onītapattapāṇino uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṁsu.
segs.e: When the senior mendicants had eaten and washed their hands and bowls, they rose from their seats and left.

segs.p: Cittopi kho gahapati “sesakaṁ vissajjethā”ti vatvā there bhikkhū piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi.
segs.e: Citta instructed that the leftovers of the food be distributed, then followed behind the senior mendicants.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena uṇhaṁ hoti kuthitaṁ;
segs.e: Now at that time it was boiling hot.

segs.p: te ca therā bhikkhū paveliyamānena maññe kāyena gacchanti, yathā taṁ bhojanaṁ bhuttāvino.
segs.e: And those senior mendicants walked along as if their bodies were melting, as happens after a meal.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahako tasmiṁ bhikkhusaṅghe sabbanavako hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Mahaka was the most junior mendicant in that Saṅgha.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahako āyasmantaṁ theraṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Mahaka said to the senior venerable,

segs.p: “sādhu khvassa, bhante thera, sītako ca vāto vāyeyya, abbhasampilāpo ca assa, devo ca ekamekaṁ phusāyeyyā”ti.
segs.e: “Wouldn’t it be nice, Honorable Senior, if a cool wind blew, a cloud canopy formed, and a gentle rain drizzled down?”

segs.p: “Sādhu khvassa, āvuso mahaka, yaṁ sītako ca vāto vāyeyya, abbhasampilāpo ca assa, devo ca ekamekaṁ phusāyeyyā”ti.
segs.e: “It would indeed be nice, Reverend Mahaka.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahako tathārūpaṁ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkhari yathā sītako ca vāto vāyi, abbhasampilāpo ca assa, devo ca ekamekaṁ phusi.
segs.e: Then Mahaka used his psychic power to will that a cool wind would blow, a cloud canopy would form, and a gentle rain would drizzle down.

segs.p: Atha kho cittassa gahapatino etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Citta thought,

segs.p: “yo kho imasmiṁ bhikkhusaṅghe sabbanavako bhikkhu tassāyaṁ evarūpo iddhānubhāvo”ti.
segs.e: “The most junior mendicant in this Saṅgha has such psychic power!”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahako ārāmaṁ sampāpuṇitvā āyasmantaṁ theraṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When they reached the monastery, Mahaka said to the senior venerable,

segs.p: “alamettāvatā, bhante therā”ti?
segs.e: “Honorable Senior, is that sufficient?”

segs.p: “Alamettāvatā, āvuso mahaka.
segs.e: “That’s sufficient, Reverend Mahaka,

segs.p: Katamettāvatā, āvuso mahaka.
segs.e: you’ve done enough

segs.p: Pūjitamettāvatā, āvuso mahakā”ti.
segs.e: and offered enough.”

segs.p: Atha kho therā bhikkhū yathāvihāraṁ agamaṁsu.
segs.e: Then the senior mendicants entered their dwellings,

segs.p: Āyasmāpi mahako sakaṁ vihāraṁ agamāsi.
segs.e: and Mahaka entered his own dwelling.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati yenāyasmā mahako tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahakaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṁ mahakaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Citta went up to Mahaka, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “sādhu me, bhante, ayyo mahako uttari manussadhammaṁ iddhipāṭihāriyaṁ dassetū”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, please show me a superhuman demonstration of psychic power.”

segs.p: “Tena hi tvaṁ, gahapati, ālinde uttarāsaṅgaṁ paññapetvā tiṇakalāpaṁ okāsehī”ti.
segs.e: “Well, then, householder, place your upper robe on the porch and spread a handful of grass on it.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho citto gahapati āyasmato mahakassa paṭissutvā ālinde uttarāsaṅgaṁ paññapetvā tiṇakalāpaṁ okāsesi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Citta, and did as he was asked.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahako vihāraṁ pavisitvā sūcighaṭikaṁ datvā tathārūpaṁ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkhari yathā tālacchiggaḷena ca aggaḷantarikāya ca acci nikkhamitvā tiṇāni jhāpesi, uttarāsaṅgaṁ na jhāpesi.
segs.e: Mahaka entered his dwelling and latched the door. Then he used his psychic power to will that a flame shoot out through the keyhole and the chink in the door-panel, and it burned up the grass but not the upper robe.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati uttarāsaṅgaṁ papphoṭetvā saṁviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then Citta shook out his upper robe and stood to one side, shocked and awestruck.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahako vihārā nikkhamitvā cittaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Mahaka left his dwelling and said to Citta,

segs.p: “alamettāvatā, gahapatī”ti?
segs.e: “Is that sufficient, householder?”

segs.p: “Alamettāvatā, bhante mahaka.
segs.e: “That’s sufficient, sir,

segs.p: Katamettāvatā, bhante, mahaka.
segs.e: you’ve done enough

segs.p: Pūjitamettāvatā, bhante mahaka.
segs.e: and offered enough.

segs.p: Abhiramatu, bhante, ayyo mahako macchikāsaṇḍe.
segs.e: I hope Master Mahaka is happy here in Macchikāsaṇḍa,

segs.p: Ramaṇīyaṁ ambāṭakavanaṁ.
segs.e: for the Wild Mango Grove is lovely.

segs.p: Ahaṁ ayyassa mahakassa ussukkaṁ karissāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānan”ti.
segs.e: I’ll make sure that Master Mahaka is provided with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.”

segs.p: “Kalyāṇaṁ vuccati, gahapatī”ti.
segs.e: “That’s nice of you to say, householder.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahako senāsanaṁ saṁsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya macchikāsaṇḍamhā pakkāmi.
segs.e: But Mahaka set his lodgings in order and, taking his bowl and robe, left Macchikāsaṇḍa,

segs.p: Yaṁ macchikāsaṇḍamhā pakkāmi, tathā pakkantova ahosi;
segs.e: never to return.

segs.p: na puna paccāgacchīti.
Catutthaṁ.

segs.p: Paṭhamakāmabhūsutta
segs.e: With Kāmabhū (1st)

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā kāmabhū macchikāsaṇḍe viharati ambāṭakavane.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Kāmabhū was staying near Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Wild Mango Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati yenāyasmā kāmabhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ kāmabhuṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho cittaṁ gahapatiṁ āyasmā kāmabhū etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Citta the householder went up to Venerable Kāmabhū, bowed, and sat down to one side. Kāmabhū said to him,

segs.p: “Vuttamidaṁ, gahapati:
segs.e: “Householder, there is this saying:

segs.p: ‘Nelaṅgo setapacchādo,
segs.e: ‘With faultless parts and white canopy,

segs.p: ekāro vattatī ratho;
segs.e: the one-spoked chariot rolls on.

segs.p: Anīghaṁ passa āyantaṁ,
segs.e: See it come, untroubled,

segs.p: chinnasotaṁ abandhanan’ti.
segs.e: with stream cut, unbound.’

segs.p: Imassa nu kho, gahapati, saṅkhittena bhāsitassa kathaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?
segs.e: How should we see the detailed meaning of this brief statement?”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho etaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā bhāsitan”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, was this spoken by the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, gahapatī”ti.
segs.e: “Yes, householder.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, bhante, muhuttaṁ āgamehi yāvassa atthaṁ pekkhāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, sir, please wait a while as I consider the meaning of this.”

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati muhuttaṁ tuṇhī hutvā āyasmantaṁ kāmabhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then after staying silent for a while, Citta said to Kāmabhū:

segs.p: “‘Nelaṅgan’ti kho, bhante, sīlānametaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: “Sir, ‘faultless parts’ is a term for ethics.

segs.p: ‘Setapacchādo’ti kho, bhante, vimuttiyā etaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘White canopy’ is a term for freedom.

segs.p: ‘Ekāro’ti kho, bhante, satiyā etaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘One spoke’ is a term for mindfulness.

segs.p: ‘Vattatī’ti kho, bhante, abhikkamapaṭikkamassetaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Rolls on’ is a term for going forward and coming back.

segs.p: ‘Ratho’ti kho, bhante, imassetaṁ cātumahābhūtikassa kāyassa adhivacanaṁ mātāpettikasambhavassa odanakummāsūpacayassa aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṁsanadhammassa.
segs.e: ‘Chariot’ is a term for this body made up of the four principal states, produced by mother and father, built up from rice and porridge, liable to impermanence, to wearing away and erosion, to breaking up and destruction.

segs.p: Rāgo kho, bhante, nīgho, doso nīgho, moho nīgho.
segs.e: Greed, hate, and delusion are troubles.

segs.p: Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: A mendicant who has ended the defilements has given these up, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, and obliterated them, so they are unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Tasmā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu ‘anīgho’ti vuccati.
segs.e: That’s why a mendicant who has ended the defilements is called ‘untroubled’.

segs.p: ‘Āyantan’ti kho, bhante, arahato etaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘The one who comes’ is a term for the perfected one.

segs.p: ‘Soto’ti kho, bhante, taṇhāyetaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Stream’ is a term for craving.

segs.p: Sā khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: A mendicant who has ended the defilements has given this up, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, and obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Tasmā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu ‘chinnasoto’ti vuccati.
segs.e: That’s why a mendicant who has ended the defilements is said to have ‘cut the stream’.

segs.p: Rāgo kho, bhante, bandhanaṁ, doso bandhanaṁ, moho bandhanaṁ.
segs.e: Greed, hate, and delusion are bonds.

segs.p: Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: A mendicant who has ended the defilements has given these up, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, and obliterated them, so they are unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Tasmā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu ‘abandhano’ti vuccati.
segs.e: That’s why a mendicant who has ended the defilements is called ‘unbound’.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhante, yaṁ taṁ bhagavatā vuttaṁ:
segs.e: So, sir, that’s how I understand the detailed meaning of what the Buddha said in brief:

segs.p: ‘Nelaṅgo setapacchādo,
segs.e: ‘With faultless parts and white canopy,

segs.p: ekāro vattatī ratho;
segs.e: the one-spoked chariot rolls on.

segs.p: Anīghaṁ passa āyantaṁ,
segs.e: See it come, untroubled,

segs.p: chinnasotaṁ abandhanan’ti.
segs.e: with stream cut, unbound.’”

segs.p: Imassa kho, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
“Lābhā te, gahapati, suladdhaṁ te, gahapati.
segs.e: “You’re fortunate, householder, so very fortunate,

segs.p: Yassa te gambhīre buddhavacane paññācakkhu kamatī”ti.
segs.e: to traverse the Buddha’s deep teachings with the eye of wisdom.”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.

segs.p: Dutiyakāmabhūsutta
segs.e: With Kāmabhū (2nd)

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā kāmabhū macchikāsaṇḍe viharati ambāṭakavane.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Kāmabhū was staying near Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Wild Mango Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati yenāyasmā kāmabhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṁ kāmabhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Citta the householder went up to Venerable Kāmabhū, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “kati nu kho, bhante, saṅkhārā”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, how many processes are there?”

segs.p: “Tayo kho, gahapati, saṅkhārā—
segs.e: “Householder, there are three processes.

segs.p: kāyasaṅkhāro, vacīsaṅkhāro, cittasaṅkhāro”ti.
segs.e: The physical process, the verbal process, and the mental process.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhante”ti kho citto gahapati āyasmato kāmabhussa bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā āyasmantaṁ kāmabhuṁ uttariṁ pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir,” Citta approved and agreed with what Kāmabhū said. Then he asked another question:

segs.p: “katamo pana, bhante, kāyasaṅkhāro, katamo vacīsaṅkhāro, katamo cittasaṅkhāro”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, what is the physical process? What’s the verbal process? What’s the mental process?”

segs.p: “Assāsapassāsā kho, gahapati, kāyasaṅkhāro, vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhāro, saññā ca vedanā ca cittasaṅkhāro”ti.
segs.e: “Breathing is a physical process. Placing the mind and keeping it connected are a verbal process. Perception and feeling are a mental process.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhante”ti kho citto gahapati …pe… uttariṁ pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir,” he asked another question:

segs.p: “kasmā pana, bhante, assāsapassāsā kāyasaṅkhāro, kasmā vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhāro, kasmā saññā ca vedanā ca cittasaṅkhāro”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, why is breathing a physical process? Why are placing the mind and keeping it connected a verbal process? Why are perception and feeling a mental process?”

segs.p: “Assāsapassāsā kho, gahapati, kāyikā. Ete dhammā kāyappaṭibaddhā, tasmā assāsapassāsā kāyasaṅkhāro.
segs.e: “Breathing is physical. It’s tied up with the body, that’s why breathing is a physical process.

segs.p: Pubbe kho, gahapati, vitakketvā vicāretvā pacchā vācaṁ bhindati, tasmā vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhāro.
segs.e: First you place the mind and keep it connected, then you break into speech. That’s why placing the mind and keeping it connected are a verbal process.

segs.p: Saññā ca vedanā ca cetasikā. Ete dhammā cittappaṭibaddhā, tasmā saññā ca vedanā ca cittasaṅkhāro”ti.
segs.e: Perception and feeling are mental. They’re tied up with the mind, that’s why perception and feeling are a mental process.”

segs.p: “Sādhu …pe… uttariṁ pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir,” he asked another question:

segs.p: “kathaṁ pana, bhante, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti hotī”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, how does someone attain the cessation of perception and feeling?”

segs.p: “Na kho, gahapati, saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjantassa bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “A mendicant who is entering such an attainment does not think:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjissan’ti vā ‘ahaṁ saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṁ saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpanno’ti vā.
segs.e: ‘I will enter the cessation of perception and feeling’ or ‘I am entering the cessation of perception and feeling’ or ‘I have entered the cessation of perception and feeling.’

segs.p: Atha khvassa pubbeva tathā cittaṁ bhāvitaṁ hoti yaṁ taṁ tathattāya upanetī”ti.
segs.e: Rather, their mind has been previously developed so as to lead to such a state.”

segs.p: “Sādhu …pe… uttariṁ pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir,” he asked another question:

segs.p: “saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjantassa pana, bhante, bhikkhuno katame dhammā paṭhamaṁ nirujjhanti, yadi vā kāyasaṅkhāro, yadi vā vacīsaṅkhāro, yadi vā cittasaṅkhāro”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, which cease first for a mendicant who is entering the cessation of perception and feeling: the physical, verbal, or mental process?”

segs.p: “Saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjantassa kho, gahapati, bhikkhuno vacīsaṅkhāro paṭhamaṁ nirujjhati, tato kāyasaṅkhāro, tato cittasaṅkhāro”ti.
segs.e: “The verbal process ceases first, then physical, then mental.”

segs.p: “Sādhu …pe… uttariṁ pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir,” he asked another question:

segs.p: “yvāyaṁ, bhante, mato kālaṅkato, yo cāyaṁ bhikkhu saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpanno, imesaṁ kiṁ nānākaraṇan”ti?
segs.e: “What’s the difference between someone who has passed away and a mendicant who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling?”

segs.p: “Yvāyaṁ, gahapati, mato kālaṅkato tassa kāyasaṅkhāro niruddho paṭippassaddho, vacīsaṅkhāro niruddho paṭippassaddho, cittasaṅkhāro niruddho paṭippassaddho, āyu parikkhīṇo, usmā vūpasantā, indriyāni viparibhinnāni.
segs.e: “When someone dies, their physical, verbal, and mental processes have ceased and stilled; their vitality is spent; their warmth is dissipated; and their faculties have disintegrated.

segs.p: Yo ca khvāyaṁ, gahapati, bhikkhu saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpanno, tassapi kāyasaṅkhāro niruddho paṭippassaddho, vacīsaṅkhāro niruddho paṭippassaddho, cittasaṅkhāro niruddho paṭippassaddho, āyu aparikkhīṇo, usmā avūpasantā, indriyāni vippasannāni.
segs.e: When a mendicant has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, their physical, verbal, and mental processes have ceased and stilled. But their vitality is not spent; their warmth is not dissipated; and their faculties are very clear.

segs.p: Yvāyaṁ, gahapati, mato kālaṅkato, yo cāyaṁ bhikkhu saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpanno, idaṁ nesaṁ nānākaraṇan”ti.
segs.e: That’s the difference between someone who has passed away and a mendicant who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling.”

segs.p: “Sādhu …pe… uttariṁ pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir,” he asked another question:

segs.p: “kathaṁ pana, bhante, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhānaṁ hotī”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, how does someone emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling?”

segs.p: “Na kho, gahapati, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahantassa bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “A mendicant who is emerging from such an attainment does not think:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahissan’ti vā ‘ahaṁ saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṁ saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhito’ti vā.
segs.e: ‘I will emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling’ or ‘I am emerging from the cessation of perception and feeling’ or ‘I have emerged from the cessation of perception and feeling.’

segs.p: Atha khvassa pubbeva tathā cittaṁ bhāvitaṁ hoti, yaṁ taṁ tathattāya upanetī”ti.
segs.e: Rather, their mind has been previously developed so as to lead to such a state.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhante …pe… uttariṁ pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir,” he asked another question:

segs.p: “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahantassa pana, bhante, bhikkhuno katame dhammā paṭhamaṁ uppajjanti, yadi vā kāyasaṅkhāro, yadi vā vacīsaṅkhāro, yadi vā cittasaṅkhāro”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, which arise first for a mendicant who is emerging from the cessation of perception and feeling: the physical, verbal, or mental process?”

segs.p: “Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahantassa, gahapati, bhikkhuno cittasaṅkhāro paṭhamaṁ uppajjati, tato kāyasaṅkhāro, tato vacīsaṅkhāro”ti.
segs.e: “The mental process arises first, then physical, then verbal.”

segs.p: “Sādhu …pe… uttariṁ pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir,” he asked another question:

segs.p: “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitaṁ pana, bhante, bhikkhuṁ kati phassā phusanti”?
segs.e: “But sir, when a mendicant has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, how many kinds of contact do they experience?”

segs.p: “Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitaṁ kho, gahapati, bhikkhuṁ tayo phassā phusanti—
segs.e: “They experience three kinds of contact:

segs.p: suññato phasso, animitto phasso, appaṇihito phasso”ti.
segs.e: emptiness, signless, and undirected contacts.”

segs.p: “Sādhu …pe… uttariṁ pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir,” he asked another question:

segs.p: “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitassa pana, bhante, bhikkhuno kiṁninnaṁ cittaṁ hoti, kiṁpoṇaṁ, kiṁpabbhāran”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, when a mendicant has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, what does their mind slant, slope, and incline to?”

segs.p: “Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitassa kho, gahapati, bhikkhuno vivekaninnaṁ cittaṁ hoti vivekapoṇaṁ vivekapabbhāran”ti.
segs.e: “Their mind slants, slopes, and inclines to seclusion.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhante”ti kho citto gahapati āyasmato kāmabhussa bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā āyasmantaṁ kāmabhuṁ uttariṁ pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir,” Citta approved and agreed with what Kāmabhū said. Then he asked another question:

segs.p: “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā pana, bhante, kati dhammā bahūpakārā”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, how many things are helpful for attaining the cessation of perception and feeling?”

segs.p: “Addhā kho tvaṁ, gahapati, yaṁ paṭhamaṁ pucchitabbaṁ taṁ pucchasi.
segs.e: “Well, householder, you’ve finally asked what you should have asked first!

segs.p: Api ca tyāhaṁ byākarissāmi.
segs.e: Nevertheless, I will answer you.

segs.p: Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā kho, gahapati, dve dhammā bahūpakārā—
segs.e: Two things are helpful for attaining the cessation of perception and feeling:

segs.p: samatho ca vipassanā cā”ti.
segs.e: serenity and discernment.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Saṁyutta Nikāya 41.7
segs.e: Linked Discourses 41.7

segs.p: 1. Cittavagga
segs.e: 1. With Citta

segs.p: Godattasutta
segs.e: With Godatta

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā godatto macchikāsaṇḍe viharati ambāṭakavane.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Godatta was staying near Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Wild Mango Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati yenāyasmā godatto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ godattaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho cittaṁ gahapatiṁ āyasmā godatto etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Citta the householder went up to Venerable Godatta, bowed, and sat down to one side. Godatta said to him:

segs.p: “yā cāyaṁ, gahapati, appamāṇā cetovimutti, yā ca ākiñcaññā cetovimutti, yā ca suññatā cetovimutti, yā ca animittā cetovimutti, ime dhammā nānatthā nānābyañjanā udāhu ekatthā byañjanameva nānan”ti?
segs.e: “Householder, the limitless release of the heart, and the release of the heart through nothingness, and the release of the heart through emptiness, and the signless release of the heart: do these things differ in both meaning and phrasing? Or do they mean the same thing, and differ only in the phrasing?”

segs.p: “Atthi, bhante, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā ca.
segs.e: “Sir, there is a way in which these things differ in both meaning and phrasing.

segs.p: Atthi pana, bhante, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nānan”ti.
segs.e: But there’s also a way in which they mean the same thing, and differ only in the phrasing.

segs.p: “Katamo ca, bhante, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā ca?
segs.e: And what’s the way in which these things differ in both meaning and phrasing?

segs.p: Idha, bhante, bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ, tathā tatiyaṁ, tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant meditates spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā …pe…
segs.e: They meditate spreading a heart full of compassion …

segs.p: muditāsahagatena cetasā …pe…
segs.e: They meditate spreading a heart full of rejoicing …

segs.p: upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ, tathā tatiyaṁ, tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: They meditate spreading a heart full of equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhante, appamāṇā cetovimutti.
segs.e: This is called the limitless release of the heart.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhante, ākiñcaññā cetovimutti?
segs.e: And what is the release of the heart through nothingness?

segs.p: Idha, bhante, bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma, ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, enters and remains in the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhante, ākiñcaññā cetovimutti.
segs.e: This is called the release of the heart through nothingness.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhante, suññatā cetovimutti?
segs.e: And what is the release of the heart through emptiness?

segs.p: Idha, bhante, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, and reflects like this:

segs.p: ‘suññamidaṁ attena vā attaniyena vā’ti.
segs.e: ‘This is empty of a self or what belongs to a self.’

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhante, suññatā cetovimutti.
segs.e: This is called the release of the heart through emptiness.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhante, animittā cetovimutti?
segs.e: And what is the signless heart’s release?

segs.p: Idha, bhante, bhikkhu sabbanimittānaṁ amanasikārā animittaṁ cetosamādhiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, not focusing on any signs, enters and remains in the signless immersion of the heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhante, animittā cetovimutti.
segs.e: This is called the signless release of the heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhante, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā ca.
segs.e: This is the way in which these things differ in both meaning and phrasing.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhante, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nānaṁ?
segs.e: And what’s the way in which they mean the same thing, and differ only in the phrasing?

segs.p: Rāgo, bhante, pamāṇakaraṇo, doso pamāṇakaraṇo, moho pamāṇakaraṇo.
segs.e: Greed, hate, and delusion are makers of limits.

segs.p: Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: A mendicant who has ended the defilements has given these up, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, and obliterated them, so they are unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Yāvatā kho, bhante, appamāṇā cetovimuttiyo, akuppā tāsaṁ cetovimutti aggamakkhāyati.
segs.e: The unshakable release of the heart is said to be the best kind of limitless release of the heart.

segs.p: Sā kho pana akuppā cetovimutti suññā rāgena, suññā dosena, suññā mohena.
segs.e: That unshakable release of the heart is empty of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: Rāgo kho, bhante, kiñcanaṁ, doso kiñcanaṁ, moho kiñcanaṁ.
segs.e: Greed is something, hate is something, and delusion is something.

segs.p: Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: A mendicant who has ended the defilements has given these up, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, and obliterated them, so they are unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Yāvatā kho, bhante, ākiñcaññā cetovimuttiyo, akuppā tāsaṁ cetovimutti aggamakkhāyati.
segs.e: The unshakable release of the heart is said to be the best kind of release of the heart through nothingness.

segs.p: Sā kho pana akuppā cetovimutti suññā rāgena, suññā dosena, suññā mohena.
segs.e: That unshakable release of the heart is empty of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: Rāgo kho, bhante, nimittakaraṇo, doso nimittakaraṇo, moho nimittakaraṇo.
segs.e: Greed, hate, and delusion are makers of signs.

segs.p: Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: A mendicant who has ended the defilements has given these up, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, and obliterated them, so they are unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Yāvatā kho, bhante, animittā cetovimuttiyo, akuppā tāsaṁ cetovimutti aggamakkhāyati.
segs.e: The unshakable release of the heart is said to be the best kind of signless release of the heart.

segs.p: Sā kho pana akuppā cetovimutti suññā rāgena, suññā dosena, suññā mohena.
segs.e: That unshakable release of the heart is empty of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhante, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nānan”ti.
segs.e: This is the way in which they mean the same thing, and differ only in the phrasing.”

segs.p: “Lābhā te, gahapati, suladdhaṁ te, gahapati.
segs.e: “You’re fortunate, householder, so very fortunate,

segs.p: Yassa te gambhīre buddhavacane paññācakkhu kamatī”ti.
segs.e: to traverse the Buddha’s deep teachings with the eye of wisdom.”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.

segs.p: Nigaṇṭhanāṭaputtasutta
segs.e: The Jain Ascetic of the Ñātika Clan

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto macchikāsaṇḍaṁ anuppatto hoti mahatiyā nigaṇṭhaparisāya saddhiṁ.
segs.e: Now at that time the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan had arrived at Macchikāsaṇḍa together with a large assembly of Jain ascetics.

segs.p: Assosi kho citto gahapati: “nigaṇṭho kira nāṭaputto macchikāsaṇḍaṁ anuppatto mahatiyā nigaṇṭhaparisāya saddhin”ti.
segs.e: Citta the householder heard that they had arrived.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati sambahulehi upāsakehi saddhiṁ yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhena nāṭaputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Together with several lay followers, he went up to the Jain Ñātika and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho cittaṁ gahapatiṁ nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. The Jain Ñātika said to him,

segs.p: “saddahasi tvaṁ, gahapati, samaṇassa gotamassa—
segs.e: “Householder, do you have faith in the ascetic Gotama’s claim that

segs.p: atthi avitakko avicāro samādhi, atthi vitakkavicārānaṁ nirodho”ti?
segs.e: there is a state of immersion without placing the mind and keeping it connected; that there is the cessation of placing the mind and keeping it connected?”

segs.p: “Na khvāhaṁ ettha, bhante, bhagavato saddhāya gacchāmi.
segs.e: “Sir, in this case I don’t rely on faith in the Buddha’s claim that

segs.p: Atthi avitakko avicāro samādhi, atthi vitakkavicārānaṁ nirodho”ti.
segs.e: there is a state of immersion without placing the mind and keeping it connected; that there is the cessation of placing the mind and keeping it connected.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto ulloketvā etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, the Jain Ñātika looked up at his assembly and said,

segs.p: “idaṁ bhavanto passantu, yāva ujuko cāyaṁ citto gahapati, yāva asaṭho cāyaṁ citto gahapati, yāva amāyāvī cāyaṁ citto gahapati, vātaṁ vā so jālena bādhetabbaṁ maññeyya, yo vitakkavicāre nirodhetabbaṁ maññeyya, sakamuṭṭhinā vā so gaṅgāya sotaṁ āvāretabbaṁ maññeyya, yo vitakkavicāre nirodhetabbaṁ maññeyyā”ti.
segs.e: “See, good sirs, how straightforward this householder Citta is! He’s not devious or deceitful at all. To imagine that you can stop placing the mind and keeping it connected would be like imagining that you can catch the wind in a net, or dam the Ganges River with your own hand.”

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, bhante,
segs.e: “What do you think, sir?

segs.p: katamaṁ nu kho paṇītataraṁ—ñāṇaṁ vā saddhā vā”ti?
segs.e: Which is better—knowledge or faith?”

segs.p: “Saddhāya kho, gahapati, ñāṇaṁyeva paṇītataran”ti.
segs.e: “Knowledge is definitely better than faith, householder.”

segs.p: “Ahaṁ kho, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: “Well sir, whenever I want, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, I enter and remain in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Ahaṁ kho, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And whenever I want, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled … I enter and remain in the second absorption.

segs.p: Ahaṁ kho, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, pītiyā ca virāgā …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And whenever I want, with the fading away of rapture … I enter and remain in the third absorption.

segs.p: Ahaṁ kho, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, sukhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And whenever I want, giving up pleasure and pain … I enter and remain in the fourth absorption.

segs.p: Na so khvāhaṁ, bhante, evaṁ jānanto evaṁ passanto kassa aññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā saddhāya gamissāmi?
segs.e: And so, sir, since I know and see like this, why should I rely on faith in another ascetic or brahmin who claims that

segs.p: Atthi avitakko avicāro samādhi, atthi vitakkavicārānaṁ nirodho”ti.
segs.e: there is a state of immersion without placing the mind and keeping it connected; that there is the cessation of placing the mind and keeping it connected?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto sakaṁ parisaṁ apaloketvā etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, the Jain Ñātika looked askance at his own assembly and said,

segs.p: “idaṁ bhavanto passantu, yāva anujuko cāyaṁ citto gahapati, yāva saṭho cāyaṁ citto gahapati, yāva māyāvī cāyaṁ citto gahapatī”ti.
segs.e: “See, good fellows, how crooked this householder Citta is! He’s so devious and deceitful!”

segs.p: “Idāneva kho te mayaṁ, bhante, bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: “Sir, just now I understood you to say:

segs.p: ‘evaṁ ājānāma idaṁ bhavanto passantu, yāva ujuko cāyaṁ citto gahapati, yāva asaṭho cāyaṁ citto gahapati, yāva amāyāvī cāyaṁ citto gahapatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘See, good fellows, how straightforward this householder Citta is! He’s not devious or deceitful at all.’

segs.p: Idāneva ca pana mayaṁ, bhante, bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: But then I understood you to say:

segs.p: ‘evaṁ ājānāma idaṁ bhavanto passantu, yāva anujuko cāyaṁ citto gahapati, yāva saṭho cāyaṁ citto gahapati, yāva māyāvī cāyaṁ citto gahapatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘See, good fellows, how crooked this householder Citta is! He’s so devious and deceitful!’

segs.p: Sace te, bhante, purimaṁ saccaṁ, pacchimaṁ te micchā.
segs.e: If your first statement is true, the second is wrong.

segs.p: Sace pana te, bhante, purimaṁ micchā, pacchimaṁ te saccaṁ.
segs.e: If your first statement is wrong, the second is true.

segs.p: Ime kho pana, bhante, dasa sahadhammikā pañhā āgacchanti.
segs.e: And also, sir, these ten legitimate questions are relevant.

segs.p: Yadā nesaṁ atthaṁ ājāneyyāsi, atha maṁ paṭihareyyāsi saddhiṁ nigaṇṭhaparisāya.
segs.e: When you understand what they mean, then, together with your assembly of Jain ascetics, you can rebut me.

segs.p: Eko pañho, eko uddeso, ekaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: ‘One thing: question, summary, and answer.

segs.p: Dve pañhā, dve uddesā, dve veyyākaraṇāni.
segs.e: Two …

segs.p: Tayo pañhā, tayo uddesā, tīṇi veyyākaraṇāni.
segs.e: Three …

segs.p: Cattāro pañhā, cattāro uddesā, cattāri veyyākaraṇāni.
segs.e: Four …

segs.p: Pañca pañhā, pañca uddesā, pañca veyyākaraṇāni.
segs.e: Five …

segs.p: Cha pañhā, cha uddesā, cha veyyākaraṇāni.
segs.e: Six …

segs.p: Satta pañhā, satta uddesā, satta veyyākaraṇāni.
segs.e: Seven …

segs.p: Aṭṭha pañhā, aṭṭha uddesā, aṭṭha veyyākaraṇāni.
segs.e: Eight …

segs.p: Nava pañhā, nava uddesā, nava veyyākaraṇāni.
segs.e: Nine …

segs.p: Dasa pañhā, dasa uddesā, dasa veyyākaraṇānī”ti.
segs.e: Ten things: question, summary, and answer.’”

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ ime dasa sahadhammike pañhe āpucchitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmīti.
segs.e: Then Citta rose from his seat and left without asking the Jain Ñātika these ten legitimate questions.

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Saṁyutta Nikāya 41.9
segs.e: Linked Discourses 41.9

segs.p: 1. Cittavagga
segs.e: 1. With Citta

segs.p: Acelakassapasutta
segs.e: With Kassapa, the Naked Ascetic

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena acelo kassapo macchikāsaṇḍaṁ anuppatto hoti cittassa gahapatino purāṇagihisahāyo.
segs.e: Now at that time the naked ascetic Kassapa, an old friend of Citta in the lay life, had arrived at Macchikāsaṇḍa.

segs.p: Assosi kho citto gahapati: “acelo kira kassapo macchikāsaṇḍaṁ anuppatto amhākaṁ purāṇagihisahāyo”ti.
segs.e: Citta the householder heard that he had arrived.

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati yena acelo kassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā acelena kassapena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: So he went up to him, and they exchanged greetings.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho citto gahapati acelaṁ kassapaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the naked ascetic Kassapa,

segs.p: “kīvaciraṁ pabbajitassa, bhante kassapā”ti?
segs.e: “Honorable Kassapa, how long has it been since you went forth?”

segs.p: “Tiṁsamattāni kho me, gahapati, vassāni pabbajitassā”ti.
segs.e: “It’s been thirty years, householder.”

segs.p: “Imehi pana te, bhante, tiṁsamattehi vassehi atthi koci uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, in these thirty years have you achieved any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable meditation?”

segs.p: “Imehi kho me, gahapati, tiṁsamattehi vassehi pabbajitassa natthi koci uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro, aññatra naggeyyā ca muṇḍeyyā ca pāvaḷanipphoṭanāya cā”ti.
segs.e: “I have no such achievement, householder, only nudity, baldness, and pokes in the buttocks.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, citto gahapati acelaṁ kassapaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Citta said to him,

segs.p: “acchariyaṁ vata, bho, abbhutaṁ vata, bho.
segs.e: “Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing,

segs.p: Dhammassa svākkhātatā yatra hi nāma tiṁsamattehi vassehi na koci uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato abhavissa phāsuvihāro, aññatra naggeyyā ca muṇḍeyyā ca pāvaḷanipphoṭanāya cā”ti.
segs.e: how well explained the teaching is. For in thirty years you have achieved no superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, no comfortable meditation, only nudity, baldness, and pokes in the buttocks.”

segs.p: “Tuyhaṁ pana, gahapati, kīvaciraṁ upāsakattaṁ upagatassā”ti?
segs.e: “But householder, how long have you been a lay follower?”

segs.p: “Mayhampi kho pana, bhante, tiṁsamattāni vassāni upāsakattaṁ upagatassā”ti.
segs.e: “It’s been thirty years, sir.”

segs.p: “Imehi pana te, gahapati, tiṁsamattehi vassehi atthi koci uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti?
segs.e: “But householder, in these thirty years have you achieved any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable meditation?”

segs.p: “Gihinopi siyā, bhante.
segs.e: “How, sir, could I not?

segs.p: Ahañhi, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: For whenever I want, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, I enter and remain in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Ahañhi, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā … dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And whenever I want, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled … I enter and remain in the second absorption.

segs.p: Ahañhi, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, pītiyā ca virāgā …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And whenever I want, with the fading away of rapture … I enter and remain in the third absorption.

segs.p: Ahañhi, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, sukhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And whenever I want, giving up pleasure and pain … I enter and remain in the fourth absorption.

segs.p: Sace kho panāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato paṭhamataraṁ kālaṁ kareyyaṁ, anacchariyaṁ kho panetaṁ yaṁ maṁ bhagavā evaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: If I pass away before the Buddha, it would be no wonder if the Buddha declares of me:

segs.p: ‘natthi taṁ saṁyojanaṁ yena saṁyojanena saṁyutto citto gahapati puna imaṁ lokaṁ āgaccheyyā’”ti.
segs.e: ‘The householder Citta is bound by no fetter that might return him to this world.’”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, acelo kassapo cittaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, Kassapa said to Citta,

segs.p: “acchariyaṁ vata bho, abbhutaṁ vata bho.
segs.e: “Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing,

segs.p: Dhammassa svākkhātatā, yatra hi nāma gihī odātavasano evarūpaṁ uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṁ adhigamissati phāsuvihāraṁ.
segs.e: how well explained the teaching is. For a white-clothed layperson can achieve such a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable meditation.

segs.p: Labheyyāhaṁ, gahapati, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye pabbajjaṁ, labheyyaṁ upasampadan”ti.
segs.e: Householder, may I receive the going forth, the ordination in this teaching and training?”

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati acelaṁ kassapaṁ ādāya yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Citta the householder took the naked ascetic Kassapa to see the senior mendicants, and said to them:

segs.p: “ayaṁ, bhante, acelo kassapo amhākaṁ purāṇagihisahāyo.
segs.e: “Sirs, this is the naked ascetic Kassapa, who in lay life was an old friend of mine.

segs.p: Imaṁ therā pabbājentu upasampādentu.
segs.e: May the senior monks give him the going forth, the ordination.

segs.p: Ahamassa ussukkaṁ karissāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānan”ti.
segs.e: I’ll make sure that he’s provided with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.”

segs.p: Alattha kho acelo kassapo imasmiṁ dhammavinaye pabbajjaṁ, alattha upasampadaṁ.
segs.e: And the naked ascetic Kassapa received the going forth, the ordination in this teaching and training.

segs.p: Acirūpasampanno ca panāyasmā kassapo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Not long after his ordination, Venerable Kassapa, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā kassapo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Kassapa became one of the perfected.

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Saṁyutta Nikāya 41.10
segs.e: Linked Discourses 41.10

segs.p: 1. Cittavagga
segs.e: 1. With Citta

segs.p: Gilānadassanasutta
segs.e: Seeing the Sick

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena citto gahapati ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: Now at that time the householder Citta was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā ārāmadevatā vanadevatā rukkhadevatā osadhitiṇavanappatīsu adhivatthā devatā saṅgamma samāgamma cittaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several deities of the parks, forests, trees, and those who haunt the herbs, grass, and big trees came together and said to Citta,

segs.p: “paṇidhehi, gahapati, anāgatamaddhānaṁ rājā assaṁ cakkavattī”ti.
segs.e: “Householder, make a wish to become a wheel-turning monarch in the future!”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, citto gahapati tā ārāmadevatā vanadevatā rukkhadevatā osadhitiṇavanappatīsu adhivatthā devatā etadavoca:
segs.e: When they said this, Citta said to them,

segs.p: “tampi aniccaṁ, tampi addhuvaṁ, tampi pahāya gamanīyan”ti.
segs.e: “That too is impermanent! That too will pass! That too will be left behind!”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, cittassa gahapatino mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā cittaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When he said this, his friends and colleagues, relatives and kin said,

segs.p: “satiṁ, ayyaputta, upaṭṭhapehi, mā vippalapī”ti.
segs.e: “Be mindful, master! Don’t babble.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ tāhaṁ vadāmi yaṁ maṁ tumhe evaṁ vadetha:
segs.e: “What have I said that makes you say that?”

segs.p: ‘satiṁ, ayyaputta, upaṭṭhapehi, mā vippalapī’”ti?
“Evaṁ kho tvaṁ, ayyaputta, vadesi:
segs.e: “It’s because you said:

segs.p: ‘tampi aniccaṁ, tampi addhuvaṁ, tampi pahāya gamanīyan’”ti.
segs.e: ‘That too is impermanent! That too will pass! That too will be left behind!’”

segs.p: “Tathā hi pana maṁ ārāmadevatā vanadevatā rukkhadevatā osadhitiṇavanappatīsu adhivatthā devatā evamāhaṁsu:
segs.e: “Oh, well, that’s because the deities of the parks, forests, trees, and those who haunt the herbs, grass, and big trees said to me:

segs.p: ‘paṇidhehi, gahapati, anāgatamaddhānaṁ rājā assaṁ cakkavattī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Householder, make a wish to become a wheel-turning monarch in the future!’

segs.p: Tāhaṁ evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: So I said to them:

segs.p: ‘tampi aniccaṁ …pe… tampi pahāya gamanīyan’”ti.
segs.e: ‘That too is impermanent! That too will pass! That too will be left behind!’”

segs.p: “Kiṁ pana tā, ayyaputta, ārāmadevatā vanadevatā rukkhadevatā osadhitiṇavanappatīsu adhivatthā devatā atthavasaṁ sampassamānā evamāhaṁsu:
segs.e: “But what reason do they see for saying that to you?”

segs.p: ‘paṇidhehi, gahapati, anāgatamaddhānaṁ rājā assaṁ cakkavattī’”ti?
“Tāsaṁ kho ārāmadevatānaṁ vanadevatānaṁ rukkhadevatānaṁ osadhitiṇavanappatīsu adhivatthānaṁ devatānaṁ evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “They think:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ kho citto gahapati, sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo.
segs.e: ‘This householder Citta is ethical, of good character.

segs.p: Sace paṇidahissati—
segs.e: If he makes a wish to

segs.p: anāgatamaddhānaṁ rājā assaṁ cakkavattī’ti, ‘tassa kho ayaṁ ijjhissati, sīlavato cetopaṇidhi visuddhattā dhammiko dhammikaṁ phalaṁ anupassatī’ti.
segs.e: become a wheel-turning monarch in the future, his heart’s wish will succeed because of the purity of his ethics. And then as a proper, principled king he will provide proper spirit-offerings.’

segs.p: Imaṁ kho tā ārāmadevatā vanadevatā rukkhadevatā osadhitiṇavanappatīsu adhivatthā devatā atthavasaṁ sampassamānā evamāhaṁsu:
segs.e: That’s the reason they see for saying to me:

segs.p: ‘paṇidhehi, gahapati, anāgatamaddhānaṁ rājā assaṁ cakkavattī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Householder, make a wish to become a wheel-turning monarch in the future!’

segs.p: Tāhaṁ evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: So I said to them:

segs.p: ‘tampi aniccaṁ, tampi addhuvaṁ, tampi pahāya gamanīyan’”ti.
segs.e: ‘That too is impermanent! That too will pass! That too will be left behind!’”

segs.p: “Tena hi, ayyaputta, amhepi ovadāhī”ti.
segs.e: “Then, master, advise us!”

segs.p: “Tasmā hi vo evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ—
segs.e: “So you should train like this:

segs.p: buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā bhavissāma:
segs.e: We will have experiential confidence in the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgatā bhavissāma:
segs.e: We will have experiential confidence in the teaching:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

segs.p: Saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgatā bhavissāma:
segs.e: We will have experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

segs.p: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṁ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segs.p: Yaṁ kho pana kiñci kule deyyadhammaṁ sabbaṁ taṁ appaṭivibhattaṁ bhavissati sīlavantehi kalyāṇadhammehīti evañhi vo sikkhitabban”ti.
segs.e: And we will share without reservation all the gifts available to give in our family with those who are ethical and of good character.”

segs.p: Atha kho citto gahapati mittāmacce ñātisālohite buddhe ca dhamme ca saṅghe ca cāge ca samādapetvā kālamakāsīti.
segs.e: Then, after Citta had encouraged his friends and colleagues, relatives and kin in the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, and generosity, he passed away.

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Cittavaggo paṭhamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Saṁyojanaṁ dve isidattā,
Mahako kāmabhūpi ca;
Godatto ca nigaṇṭho ca,
Acelena gilānadassananti.
Cittasaṁyuttaṁ samattaṁ.
segs.e: The Linked Discourses on Citta the Householder are complete.
